## Problem and intended result

The sitting found batted balls and throws too fast to read. Establish the game's long-term compact-field proportions, ball motion and race pacing by comparing Mario Super Sluggers (Wii), Mario Superstar Baseball (GameCube), and the inspected Harbor baseline. A routine hopper should produce a readable pickup/throw/runner race; outfield travel should register visibly; compact cartoon space must preserve doubles, triples and useful relays.

This is a researched gameplay contract, followed by coordinated calibration. Do not shrink one mesh, special-case a play, tune one seed into passing, or treat green CI as human acceptance. Sim owns geometric outcomes; presentation follows the shared rules. Reference measurements, community reports, authored trials and simulated evidence must stay distinct.

## Current decisions and authoritative records

Jack is resolving required decisions **one at a time**. Full accepted scopes, numbers, alternatives, evidence limits and pending work are version-controlled:

- [Decision register and execution plan](https://github.com/jackguillet/grand-sluggers/blob/59baf8c/docs/plan-game-feel-693.md)
- [Current compact-field research/decision report](https://github.com/jackguillet/grand-sluggers/blob/59baf8c/docs/research-game-feel-708.md)
- [Machine-readable candidate and approval provenance](https://github.com/jackguillet/grand-sluggers/blob/59baf8c/docs/research/game-feel-708-candidates.json)
- [Gameplay spec D19](https://github.com/jackguillet/grand-sluggers/blob/59baf8c/docs/gameplay-spec.md)

Accepted highlights: Wii provisional visual lead with GameCube mechanics cross-check; C80 first spatial trial (80-foot paths, 232/280/232-foot fences, unchanged characters); preserved runner elapsed pace; quick visible release and readable flight; reliable ordinary defense; distinct contact classes; moderate ball-readability assistance and deliberately readable result beats. Compactness is coordinated with movement/ball/throw budgets, not rescued through an enormous outfield.

Numerical trials include .30 ordinary release, .90 neutral Field-5 flight over 80 feet, the documented arm-dependent long-range curve and per-leg chemistry; deliberate commands per relay leg, scoped Snap Throw/Laser, .25 input buffer and contextual cancel. Movement includes Run-5 18 ft/s, accepted positional reads, .20 acceleration/.10 braking, continuous angled response and full reversal, radial proportional analog speed and .20 manual entry/.15 assisted exit. The report defines exact scope and exceptions; these highlights are not a substitute contract.

**Latest direction / correction — simple arcade fielding:** Jack directed F693-02-arcade-fielding-simplification on September 15, 2026: this is cartoon toy baseball. Resolve fielding through explicit character range, ball trajectory, readiness and existing error rules; make the glove pocket face the ball visually. Detailed pocket/rim/back collision, contact normals and glove-facing gates are not required. Retire F693-02-error-contact-obstruction-basis, F693-02-glove-contact-surface, the pending F693-02-glove-catch-sides, and the geometry-dependent retention curve as mandatory runtime contracts. Preserve prior numeric response trials, including the 50–80% continuing bounds, errors, stun, recovery and specials. A presentation mismatch must not create an extra miss. No runtime/asset change or human gate pass.

**Next research action — no pending glove microdecision:** F693-02-arcade-fielding-validation: consolidate the simple range/readiness contract and representative catches, bobbles and hard infield escapes; compare both references with evidence labels and identify the next material gameplay tradeoff. Keep human decisions one at a time, but stop the hidden glove-microphysics approval chain. No replacement glove question awaits approval. Simplified response mapping, range dimensions, traits, coverage, ordinary ball calibration and full race validation remain open. Recorded at `59baf8c`.

Historical Harbor misses remain open; do not pool them away. Named routine-defense cases, full runner/glove/ball/receiver races and independent validation are required. Parent: #693. Session kind: **Gameplay research/documentation**. Stacked after #702 / draft #707; this child is draft #709. **Keep this issue open through the complete contract and Jack’s standalone feel acceptance.**

## Problem and intended result

Define compact-field proportions and coordinated movement/ball/throw timing so Harbor feels like a readable cartoon baseball game with reliable routine defense, doubles, triples and useful relays. Compare Wii and GameCube references before choosing; separate reference observations, community claims, authored trials, arithmetic and actual simulated results. Do not tune one fixture, enlarge the field to rescue its clocks, or claim green CI passes a human gate.

## Current decisions and authoritative records

Jack resolves decisions one at a time. Exact scopes and history live in the versioned records:

- [Current research/decision report](https://github.com/jackguillet/grand-sluggers/blob/59baf8c/docs/research-game-feel-708.md)
- [Decision register and implementation plan](https://github.com/jackguillet/grand-sluggers/blob/59baf8c/docs/plan-game-feel-693.md)
- [Candidate values and approval provenance](https://github.com/jackguillet/grand-sluggers/blob/59baf8c/docs/research/game-feel-708-candidates.json)
- [Derived arithmetic and source hashes](https://github.com/jackguillet/grand-sluggers/blob/59baf8c/docs/research/game-feel-708-derived.json)
- [Gameplay spec D19](https://github.com/jackguillet/grand-sluggers/blob/59baf8c/docs/gameplay-spec.md)

Accepted: C80 spatial trial (80-foot paths, 232/280/232-foot fences, unchanged character bodies); preserved runner elapsed pace; .30 ordinary release and .90 neutral Field-5 flight over 80 feet; authored long-range curve, per-leg good/bad chemistry, deliberate relay commands, scoped Snap Throw/Laser, .25 input buffer and contextual cancel. Ordinary pursuit Run-5 18 ft/s and positional reads, physical start/stop/turn/analog response, calibrated input and arming are recorded individually.

The universal activated fielding sprint and two-second burst were superseded after Jack redirected dash: **passive Ball Dash adds 20% only for ability holders securely carrying the ball**, with no activation/timer/cooldown. Ordinary carrying equals ordinary pursuit speed; acceleration/braking stay based on unboosted character speed. Character allocation remains a separate decision; no current record has Ball Dash. The complete report, not these highlights, is the contract.

**Latest direction / correction — simple arcade fielding:** Jack directed F693-02-arcade-fielding-simplification on September 15, 2026: this is cartoon toy baseball. Resolve fielding through explicit character range, ball trajectory, readiness and existing error rules; make the glove pocket face the ball visually. Detailed pocket/rim/back collision, contact normals and glove-facing gates are not required. Retire F693-02-error-contact-obstruction-basis, F693-02-glove-contact-surface, the pending F693-02-glove-catch-sides, and the geometry-dependent retention curve as mandatory runtime contracts. Preserve prior numeric response trials, including the 50–80% continuing bounds, errors, stun, recovery and specials. A presentation mismatch must not create an extra miss. No runtime/asset change or human gate pass.

**Latest approvals — the fielding contract is decided (September 15):** F693-02-arcade-fielding-validation is research complete; the report states the simplified contract end to end across a routine grounder, an awkward in-between hop and a hard infield ball that escapes, and both reference clips are clean fielding, so the error behaviour has no matched Wii or GameCube observation. **F693-02-catch-reach-envelope:** the ordinary stand-up catch reach is re-authored to roughly 6 feet, over keeping 13 and over scaling to 11.56; third-to-short reopens to 1.46 seconds, short-to-second to 2.09 and the alley to 2.56. **F693-02-dive-jump-scoop-reach:** the dive fired automatically whenever the seat's stick was neutral and unconditionally for the CPU-driven glove, making 6 feet plus an automatic 8 into 14 feet of passive coverage, more than the 13 removed. The assistance dive is gone — a dive happens only on a deliberate press, passive coverage is 6 feet in the air and 10 on the dirt, an earned dive reaches 14 — and a dive now carries a recovery delay before the diver can throw or move. **F693-02-cpu-dive-intent:** the CPU glove dives deliberately, **it can miss**, it pays the same delay and reaches the same 14 feet. The convert-only option was explicitly declined, so a failed CPU dive is required behaviour. **F693-02-dive-recovery-cost:** the delay is **.60 seconds** at the lowest defensive quality, narrowing 2.5% per point to .465 at the highest — derived from the illustrative routine race, whose .50-second margin makes .60 the shortest value at which an unnecessary dive costs the out. Deliberately narrower than the recoil curve, so even the best defender only reaches a dead heat. Caught and missed dives cost the same, and the delay overlaps the .40-second handling stun rather than adding, a recorded departure from the additive precedent. **Correction on the record:** the sim runs exactly one active glove handed on as the play develops, not nine chasers; earlier wording about eight fielders diving automatically was wrong and is corrected in the report and appended to the tracker. Findings and decisions are unaffected. **F693-02-defensive-trait-mapping:** the required inventory found `Stats.Field` driving four distinct jobs — arm (throw speed, comfortable range, accuracy), hands (recoil duration, error chance, dive recovery), reach (already leaving) and three CPU-only reaction timings that are difficulty scaling wearing a character stat. The displayed Fielding number was simultaneously the arm rating and the hands rating, so a cannon-armed catcher with stone hands could not exist. **Jack split Arm out:** Arm is the throwing rating, Fielding becomes the hands rating, reach belongs to neither, and every character's Arm is seeded from their current Field value so all accepted throw anchors evaluate identically on day one. Recorded knock-ons: the content schema gains Arm; **whether Arm joins the `Teams.Tools` roster-building sum is a deliberate choice, not automatic**; the HUD gains an A and displayed Fielding now means hands only; and the CPU reaction timings default to Fielding with their character-driven-ness still open. **Correction on the record:** the sim runs exactly one active glove handed on as the play develops, not nine chasers; earlier wording about eight fielders diving automatically was wrong and is corrected in the report and appended to the tracker. **F693-04-flight-budget:** measured from the game's own model and cross-checked against `BallFlight.CarryFeet` within 0.7 foot, **C80 as specified was a home-run derby** — a Power-3 bat crossed centre field at 12.2 feet on a charged perfect swing and a Power-10 bat crossed the pole at 17.1 feet on ordinary uncharged line-drive contact, both comfortably in play on the control field. The doubles engine turns out to be the liner, not the fly: `linerTimeScale 1.0` keeps liners on the real clock at 1.8–3.3 seconds against the 2.56-second alley closure while flies hang 4.3–8.5 seconds and are always caught, so the risk to gap hits is that liners clear the fence, not that they get caught. **Jack raised the ball's drag from .0019 to a .0040 trial**, leaving the exit table and the 12-foot wall untouched: ordinary contact stays in the park, a charged squared-up mid-power swing clears the pole but not centre, the biggest bat clears centre, star swings clear centre reliably, and gap doubles go up. **The drag change cannot ship alone** — drag is global and the other five parks are still at control scale, where .0040 leaves no home runs at all, so the ball change and the park migration must land together. **F693-02-coverage-budget:** cover, cutoff and backup all moved through `StepFlat` at a flat 28 ft/s with no acceleration or character difference, so the same body ran 56% faster to a bag than to a ball. **Jack made covering bodies inherit the accepted 18 ft/s profile**, beginning at contact with no read, since covering is a known assignment rather than the recognition of where a batted ball went; the accepted pursuit reads are unchanged and the double-play feed keeps +0.39 s on an average ball and +0.09 on a quick one. Not at risk and not to be re-litigated: the cutoff, the relay (4.00 s against a 4.80 s direct throw), and receiver reach, `cover.radiusFt` 6 now matching the accepted 6-foot stand-up reach. **Step 3a is complete.** Park and Arm migration consolidated: every fence scales by 0.70 with Harbor keeping its accepted 232/280/232, wall heights unscaled, hazards scaled by the zone they sit in; Arm is seeded from Field and excluded from `Teams.Tools` through the parity slice, since while the two are equal including it double-counts defence. Basepath is **not** a park property and `Diamond` is a C# constant, so C80 is one change and moving the diamond into data is the parity slice's first commit. **F693-02-cpu-dive-intent-policy:** lookahead was not the question — the route planner already returns `MissFt` and already sees the whole trajectory — the problem was that a CPU diving on it would essentially always reach. **Jack made the CPU dive decision read the ball's live position and motion at the instant it commits**, so a late bounce, carom or deflection beats it and a CPU dive misses because the world moved rather than because a roll said so; ordinary CPU pursuit keeps the route planner. **Next:** 3b, the parity slice. **Pending:** F693-02-throw-before-cover, plus special attacks, movement response and presentation, all outside the sequence. No rules file, runtime, roster or human gate change. Recorded at `3afcfca`.

The earlier detailed glove geometry, incidence, catch-side and geometry-dependent interpolation decisions below are historical and superseded by F693-02-arcade-fielding-simplification. See the current-direction section of the report. No glove microdecision is pending. F693-02-arcade-fielding-validation is now research complete, and the eight human decisions it raised are accepted: **F693-02-catch-reach-envelope** re-authors the ordinary stand-up catch reach to roughly 6 feet, **F693-02-dive-jump-scoop-reach** makes the dive earned-only with a recovery delay, **F693-02-cpu-dive-intent** gives the CPU glove deliberate dive intent at the same cost, **F693-02-dive-recovery-cost** sets that delay at .60 seconds on a narrow character curve, **F693-02-defensive-trait-mapping** splits Arm out of the Fielding rating, **F693-04-flight-budget** raises the ball's drag to a .0040 trial, **F693-02-coverage-budget** puts covering bodies on the same movement profile as everyone else, and **F693-02-cpu-dive-intent-policy** makes the CPU dive decision read the live ball. Issue #693 needs a compact field with readable races, reliable routine defense, doubles, triples and relays. This research packet compares C80/C70 with the historical control and records the accepted C80 spatial trial: 80-foot bases, 232/280/232-foot fences and unchanged characters. It separates reference observations, authored targets and arithmetic from simulated results.

Accepted ordinary anchors: existing runner elapsed pace and stat/dash schedule; .30-second release; .90-second neutral Field-5 flight over 80 feet; and the arm-dependent long-range curve with 160-foot middle comfortable range. Good/bad actual-pair travel factors are 1.30/.90, with the extra bad-chemistry slant removed as the target rule. Snap Throw becomes a .22-second release after clean teammate-throw reception; Laser becomes a 1.25x flight factor on eligible actual throws home. Exact scopes, stacking, evidence limits and roster costs are documented.

Accepted human relay controls require one deliberate command per leg, a .25-second early-input buffer, and contextual RB/period cancel with existing bag controls for retargeting. Selected versus queued feedback, input precedence, expiry and seat/receiver binding are explicit. Runtime/book controls are unchanged here.

Accepted movement trials: Run-5 ordinary pursuit top speed 18 ft/s with the existing relative character-speed curve, one profile across positions/hit types; .40-second base outfield read from contact without an extra camera wait. Jack also accepted shared .25-second read for 1B/2B/SS/3B. Jack also accepted .35-second base pitcher read from contact, with explicit delivery/camera boundaries and comebacker/bunt validation requirements. Jack also accepted .45-second catcher pursuit read after batted contact, with no additional wait on steal throws or home receptions. Jack also accepted a linear .20-second ordinary pursuit build-up from rest, shared duration across characters at their respective top speeds, with prediction/stepping parity and no selection-based ramp reset. Jack also accepted linear braking from full ordinary speed to rest in .10 seconds, shorter stops from partial speed, and planned assisted arrival without changing neutral-stick assistance or moving-catch eligibility. Jack also accepted full reversal through the approved brake/start, reaching opposite full speed in .30 seconds without an extra pivot pause or command lock. Jack also accepted continuous angled correction through the same rates, with .115-second/92.4% minimum-speed behavior at 45 degrees and .212-second/70.7% at 90 degrees. The shared velocity rule preserves the accepted start/stop/reversal and ordinary speed cap. Jack also accepted linear speed across active radial stick travel for fine pursuit. Jack also accepted calibrated radial manual entry at .20 and exit to assistance at .15, retaining ownership in between and mapping manual speed from .15. Jack also accepted fixed per-device pursuit calibration during a match, established from released controls outside live play, with explicit paused recalibration. Jack also accepted neutral readiness at defensive-role/device/calibration boundaries, retained through the half for held direction at contact. Jack approved F693-02-pursuit-calibration-samples: a .50-second valid released-stick calibration window, mean radial center offset <=.10 and every sample within .02 of that mean. Inclusive bounds, complete-window stability and monotonic non-live input time; failed sampling preserves the prior valid profile. Calibration only, with no extra routine arming delay. These authored bounds still require real controller validation. Jack approved F693-02-ball-dash-carrier: automatic 1.20x ordinary carrying speed only for an ability holder securely possessing the live ball, for human and CPU fielders alike. No activation input, burst timer, stamina or cooldown. This supersedes universal fielding sprint and its earlier two-second approval; preserve their history. Ordinary pursuit before possession and separate baserunning anchors remain intact. Jack approved F693-02-ordinary-carry-speed: ordinary carrying top speed equals each character’s ordinary pursuit speed, without a generic possession penalty/bonus. Run-5 is 18 ft/s, or 21.6 with the separately accepted passive Ball Dash. Same carrying context for both seats, CPU movement and forecasts. Response, recovery, coverage and roster remain separate. Jack approved F693-02-carry-movement-response: shared ordinary acceleration/braking/continuous-turn law for eligible carrying, with rates based on unboosted character speed during Ball Dash. Ordinary start/stop/reverse remain .20/.10/.30 seconds; boosted equivalents are .24/.12/.36. Preserve actual velocity and share prediction/stepping. Recovery/eligibility, coverage and roster remain separate. Jack approved F693-02-clean-ground-pickup-readiness: zero generic pause after a routine clean ground/loose pickup is securely possessed and no exceptional recovery is active. Continue eligible carrying or begin ordinary .30-second release when a valid deliberate/buffered command is ready. Preserve visible acquisition, geometry, queue expiry/cancellation, and real recovery; no automatic throw or Snap Throw pickup bonus. Jack approved F693-02-ground-pickup-recoil-basis on September 15, 2026: deterministic ordinary retained-ball ground-pickup recoil from actual incoming world-space ball speed at acquisition and Field rating, with correct gameplay clock/event ordering. Slower arrival or higher Field cannot worsen recoil; routine arrivals have zero recovery. Original hit/contact labels do not independently cause it. Thresholds, curve/cap, Field scaling, physical reaction and permissions remain separate. Jack accepted F693-02-ground-pickup-recoil-cap on September 15, 2026 with an explicit condition: .20 seconds caps ordinary retained-ball recoil, while authored special hits may exceed it through their own recovery rules. No global clamp on special stuns/knockback. Routine arrivals remain zero; the cap is not a fixed pause or permission to exempt ordinary Perfect/charged hits. Special values, onset/curve/Field mapping and physical/action recovery remain open. Jack approved F693-02-special-recovery-composition on September 15, 2026: add ordinary Field-dependent recoil and authored special recovery from the same pickup/impact, preserving the ordinary recovery difference. Cap ordinary contribution at .20, not the special or total. Count applicable event/action contributions once; unrelated/earlier/repeated effects, multiple-special behavior and actual action permissions remain separate. Prior unaccepted overlap proposal stays in candidate history. Jack approved F693-02-recoil-field-shaping on September 15, 2026: shared incoming-speed onset, with Field shortening ordinary recovery after speed severity is bounded. Structure .20*S(speed)*F(Field) preserves distinct Field factors even at maximum severity. Add applicable special recovery afterward. Numeric thresholds, severity curve and Field factors remain separate; no runtime changes. Jack approved F693-02-recoil-field-factors on September 15, 2026: F(Field)=1-.05*(Field-1) on validated Field1..10. Maximum ordinary recoil .20/.16/.12/.11 at Field1/5/9/10, proportionally shorter at lesser severity. Apply the factor only to ordinary recoil before adding same-impact special recovery; ratings and throw release remain unchanged. Severity curve and physical speed anchors remain separate. Jack approved F693-02-recoil-severity-curve on September 15, 2026: linear S(v)=clamp((v-v0)/(v1-v0),0,1) between shared incoming-speed anchors, zero below onset and full above the upper anchor. Apply the accepted Field factor after bounded severity, then applicable same-impact special recovery. v0/v1 remain null pending event-sided arrival evidence and coherent ball-motion calibration. Jack approved F693-02-ordinary-recoil-actions on September 15, 2026: ordinary retained-ball recoil blocks commanded locomotion/steering and throw starts while preserving secure possession, valid geometric forces/tags, and responsive buffer/cancel/target management. Actual contact governs outs; no precharge, Ball Dash bypass or world freeze. Physical recoil and special permissions remain separate. Jack approved F693-02-ordinary-recoil-displacement on September 15, 2026: modest physical pushback on qualifying ordinary retained-ball ground pickups, including loss of bag/tag contact, with special emphasis on special hits that impact the fielder. Routine zero-recoil pickups add no shove. Use actual incoming horizontal direction and integrated body/glove movement; preserve existing velocity and legally completed outs. Impacting specials can author stronger displacement and longer recovery; this does not grant every special knockback or define impulse stacking. Jack approved F693-02-ordinary-recoil-distance-cap on September 15, 2026: one foot maximum added ordinary impact displacement, with routine pickups at zero and lesser impacts below the ceiling. This caps the ordinary impact component, not total travel from existing momentum. Special hits that impact the fielder may exceed it under their own finite authored bounds. Exact motion response remains separately reviewed. Jack approved F693-02-ordinary-recoil-motion-profile on September 15, 2026: a brief impact kick slowing linearly to zero over ordinary recovery, with stronger Fielding reducing displacement as well as recovery time. Let w=S(arrivalSpeed)*F(Field); T=.20w seconds, D=w squared feet and initial added speed K=10w ft/s. Preserve and brake existing locomotion with unboosted b=V/.10; integrate one actual body/glove path without teleport or an extra wait to stop. Incoming-speed anchors and special motion remain separately reviewed. Jack approved F693-02-special-impact-motion-composition on September 15, 2026: concurrent ordinary and authored special pushback from the same retained-ball pickup/impact, each counted once in one authoritative body/glove path. Preserve separate motion clocks, directions and finite bounds, ordinary Field-dependent motion and the accepted additive per-action recovery. No global one-foot clamp on special motion, ordinary timer stretch, duplicate restart or restoration of steering while special recovery still blocks it. Individual special strength/resistance and repeated-effect rules remain separate. Jack approved F693-02-special-impact-field-resistance on September 15, 2026: R(Field)=1-.20*(Field-1)/9 reduces the special physical displacement and associated impact recovery from 100 percent at Field1 to 80 percent at Field10. Apply once to the special component before composition; ordinary recoil retains its separate factor. Retiming finite impact velocity as v_base(t/R) preserves peak speed while reducing travel and duration. Non-impact statuses, immunity, exceptions and individual attack contracts remain separately reviewed. Jack approved F693-02-special-pushback-possession on September 15, 2026: pure special pushback preserves an already-secured ball without an added random drop roll. Existing catch failures/bobbles remain; an explicitly authored dislodging effect can produce a real loose ball under its own reviewed conditions. Resolve acquisition/loss before exposing secure ownership or a possession-dependent out. Actual later loss invalidates ownership-bound commands without reversing earlier legal outs. Special action permissions remain separate. Jack approved F693-02-special-pushback-actions on September 15, 2026: pure special pushback uses ordinary recoil permissions, blocking commanded steering and throw starts through the applicable recovery while preserving valid held-ball forces/tags and responsive buffer/cancel/target management. Keep the accepted combined recovery, .25-second command expiry and live physical movement. A legally completed force is not reversed by later pushback. Other status interactions remain separately reviewed. Jack approved F693-02-mixed-status-action-readiness on September 15, 2026: restore each action when normal prerequisites hold and no active effect still restricts it. Expiring a source clears only its own restrictions; unrelated lingering effects do not create a blanket character lock. Preserve the accepted same-impact ordinary-plus-special recovery sum before evaluating other sources. Eligibility does not auto-throw, award outs, refresh the input buffer or bypass another status. Jack approved F693-02-repeated-impact-recovery on September 15, 2026: start each distinct physical impact recovery at its arrival, with each action blocked through the latest applicable end. Do not queue the new full duration after the unfinished wait or truncate an older restriction with a weaker hit. Ordinary and Field-resisted special recovery from the same qualifying event still add first. Preserve event/source identities, unchanged buffer age and separate rules for hit eligibility, repeated impulses and anti-chain limits. Jack approved F693-02-special-impact-repeat-eligibility on September 15, 2026: one physical hit per fielder per special activation by default, with explicitly reviewed multi-hit exceptions. Continued contact, genuine re-entry, bounce, drop/reacquisition or control switching cannot retrigger that activation on the same fielder. Another fielder may receive a first qualifying impact only while the authored attack remains active; a genuinely new activation may hit the original fielder. Ordinary acquisition recoil and other reviewed effect components remain separate. Multi-hit limits, repeated impulses and independent-attack chains remain pending. Jack approved F693-02-clean-air-catch-readiness on September 15, 2026: zero generic added pause after a clean routine airborne batted-ball catch by a grounded fielder. Once secure possession exists and no applicable recovery blocks the action, eligible movement or a valid ordinary .30-second throw release may begin while play stays live. Preserve visible acquisition, actual carrying velocity, .25-second buffer/cancel behavior and caught-ball/retouch/tag-up/force-removal/play-end rules. No instant catch, extra reach, automatic throw or Snap Throw from a batted catch. Exceptional catches remain separately reviewed.
